 iShares PHLX SOX Semiconductor Sector Index Fund ( SOXX ) extended its recent run of broad accumulation on Monday, Oct. 26, buying $196.8 million of stock and selling none. SOXX increased all 30 of its positions, with no decreases, in a day of one-way ETF activity .

 What did SOXX buy on Monday? 
 Its largest buys by dollar value were AMD ($18.3 million), INTC ($16.4 million) and NVDA ($15.9 million).

 The largest buy was Advanced Micro Devices, with 34,512 shares added for $18.3 million, lifting its weight to 9.32%. Intel followed with 181,480 shares bought for $16.4 million, then NVIDIA with 73,576 shares for $15.9 million, Micron Technology with 16,944 shares for $15.3 million and Broadcom with 43,864 shares for $14.4 million. None of the buys was a new position and there were no exits. 
 How does SOXX invest? 
 SOXX is an equity sector information technology fund holding 30 stocks, with 62.7% of assets in its 10 largest holdings. Technology accounts for 100.0% of the stocks that could be classified, and the portfolio is 100.0% large-cap. It charges 0.33% and its top holdings are Advanced Micro Devices at 9.32%, Intel at 8.34%, NVIDIA at 8.07%, Micron Technology at 7.78% and Broadcom at 7.34%. The fund has a GF Score of 86, a P/E of 44.13, a P/B of 11.62, a dividend yield of 0.25% and a year-to-date return of 70.0%.
